title: A Survey on Evaluation of Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: The paper reviews literature that evaluates gender bias by calculating fairness metrics like Demographic Parity Difference (DPD) and Equalized Odds Difference (EOD) across genders, as well as using datasets to gauge stereotype bias via targeted system prompts.

The survey summarizes studies that measure racial bias by assessing stereotypes towards specific racial groups using conventional testing sets, and by calculating fairness metrics (DPD and EOD) across different racial demographics.
The paper reviews evaluations that test for social biases and stereotypes directed towards individuals based on their religion, utilizing prompt-based testing and stereotype evaluation datasets.

The survey discusses methodologies that assess ideological tendencies in models by administering standardized questionnaires, such as the Political Compass Test, to measure the model's political views and moral biases.

The paper reviews multilingual evaluations that identify "English bias," where models demonstrate significantly poorer performance, neutrality, and impartiality when processing non-Latin scripts and low-resource languages compared to English.
The survey summarizes empirical studies that assess how models align with specific cultural values, noting biases that emerge when models are evaluated against diverse societal norms.

The paper highlights literature measuring age bias through automated fairness evaluations, specifically checking if model performance remains equal across age groups using Demographic Parity Difference.
The survey references methodologies that evaluate stereotype biases regarding occupations, utilizing datasets with targeted and untargeted prompts to measure biased associations.
